basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 22.' and it opens '(Vers. 22.) Et dixit Abimelech et Ochozath pronubus ejus, et Phicol princeps exercitus'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 22.) Et dixit Abimelech et Ochozath pronubus ejus, et Phicol princeps exercitus ejus. Excepto Abimelech et Phicol, tertium nomen, quod hic legitur, in Hebraeo volumine non habetur.
